#### Level2 and UnitedHealth Group: buyer, scope, procurement

- **Buyer.** Level2 calls itself "a UnitedHealthcare company" (LinkedIn) and "a UHG Ventures Company" (its Senior Director of Implementation's headline), and runs with its own CEO (James Conlin), COO (Libby MacFarlane), CPO (Kori Heinen) and National Medical Director (David Ferrell), all in the export. They own the member app and the clinical model, so they are the buyer for anything inside the Level2 experience.
- **No UHG-level contacts in this campaign.** The only UnitedHealth Group row is Kori Heinen, who is Level2's CPO. UnitedHealthcare, UHG and Optum corporate roles are a different segment (`icp-detail.md` lists UnitedHealthcare under insurance underwriting and plan wellness), a different buyer (enterprise procurement, population health, wellness) and a different program set: UnitedHealthcare runs separate weight programs ([Real Appeal](https://www.uhc.com/member-resources/wellness-rewards-programs/real-appeal), [Total Weight Support](https://www.uhc.com/news-articles/benefits-and-coverage/total-weight-support)). A UnitedHealthcare-level approach is its own future campaign, informed by what Level2 says. Level2 copy stays on Level2's program.
- **Procurement caveats.**
  1. Any contract is a UnitedHealthcare vendor contract: expect a formal third-party security review and a BAA for member photos and outputs. A SOC 2 report is commonly requested in such reviews and 3DLOOK can only say it "is working toward obtaining a SOC 2 Attestation Report and has completed an initial readiness assessment" (`compliance.md`). Third-party security has been under heightened scrutiny at UHG since the February 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack ([UNH 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176624000323/unh-20240930.htm), [AHA](https://www.aha.org/aha-center-health-innovation-market-scan/2024-10-22-4-keys-manage-third-party-cybersecurity-risk)).
  2. Level2 is free to members; employers pay, and under the Level2 Assured Value Program employers with more than 125 covered employees are refunded if program fees exceed medical and pharmacy savings (UHG 2025 brief). Any per-scan cost lands inside that guarantee.
  3. Member-facing changes go through UnitedHealthcare brand and legal review. The realistic 8-week outcome at Level2 is a discovery call, not a pilot.
  4. Registry: record the company as Level2 (linkedin.com/company/mylevel2), never UnitedHealth Group, so a later UnitedHealthcare campaign does not read UHG as already contacted.

#### Signos: why it is held

The campaign's use case ("add body data beyond glucose, inside the app, no device") went live at Signos in July 2026 with another vendor. A cold message cannot offer Signos members anything they do not already have, and on outputs FitXpress publishes less than members see today (no visceral fat, no appendicular lean mass in `proof-points.md`). There is no head-to-head study to argue repeatability or accuracy against their current scan. **Default: not sent, not registered, so the account stays free for a later approach on a trigger** (a vendor change, a body-scan job posting, the scan appearing in Signos's employer reporting). If Vadim releases it (Open question 1), all 20 people already have tiers and lanes below and the displacement rules in "Rules for steps 3-5" apply. Separately, Signos markets an FDA-cleared glucose system; FitXpress copy to anyone never mentions FDA.

**KPIs they care about:** what the program can show an employer or plan beyond weight and A1c (body composition, waist, durability); member engagement between visits or lab draws; device logistics and cost; for 9amHealth, safer GLP-1 prescribing and what its new body-composition scales cover; for Level2, progress through its phases and total cost of care against its savings guarantee; for Superpower, what changes between the two draws and renewal of the membership.

**Likely objections and the honest answer:**
- "Our scale already measures body composition" (9amHealth). The scan returns what none of 9amHealth's announced devices is described as returning: waist, hip and other circumferences, and a 3D model, in the 9am app. Its body composition estimates are a different method and sit alongside the scale; there is no head-to-head study against BIA or DXA to quote, and a pilot can compare both in the same members. Never improvise numbers.
- "We already offer DEXA" (Superpower). DEXA stays the method wherever a member books it. The scan is a home capture between lab draws for waist, hip and a 3D model; there is no published comparison of its body composition estimates with DEXA, and none is claimed.
- "We are a glucose program" (Level2). Waist circumference and glucose are both cardiometabolic risk markers (Lancet Commission; IAS/ICCR); this says nothing about what Level2 records today. The scan is an optional capture in the member's app, not a new device. Whether it belongs in a phase is a pilot question.
- "We are blood-first" (Superpower). Its own guide lists waist-to-hip ratio and lean mass as biomarkers; the scan captures the inputs at home between draws.
- "How accurate is it?" "96-97% accuracy against expert manual measurement" (body measurements, not body composition), or the full sentence from `accuracy-formulations.md` §1.1; repeatability as the §1.2 sentence; validation population 38-210 kg. Performance outside that scope has not been characterized.
- "HIPAA? SOC 2? FDA?" HIPAA: the US compliance line. SOC 2, verbatim: "3DLOOK is working toward obtaining a SOC 2 Attestation Report and has completed an initial readiness assessment aligned with SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria." FDA, verbatim from the live trust FAQ: "FitXpress is not cleared, authorized, or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). 3DLOOK makes no representation as to whether FDA clearance, authorization, or approval is required for any particular customer's use case." "FitXpress is not a medical device." rests on the UK/EU MDR assessment and is never an answer to an FDA question.
- "Security review, vendor onboarding" (Level2 above all). Security overview on request; architecture, pen-test summary, incident-response and BC/DR summaries under NDA; DPA and BAA in contracting; requests to legal@3dlook.me.
- "Our roadmap is full." API and SDK into the existing app; 2-4 weeks for a typical basic integration (a generic figure, never a promise).

### Anti-cases (where it does NOT work)

- **Held, by name:** Signos (in-app phone body composition scanning live since July 2026; displacement).
- **Out, by name:** the export rows for Level2 Cable Solutions, IGC SuperPower, Superpower Planner, Turbo Tim's Anything Automotive (Superpower Innovators), Picogrid, Belief Capital, Myo, Aquivia Health, Commonwealth Sterile Solutions, Effecty, MetaphysicalMBA, and the "Signos" row with no company page (edgar tudela). University of Oxford, Prime Healthcare, Meliora Integrative Medicine and AMR Clinical are out as companies; their one person each moves to an in-scope account (verdict table).
- **Structural anti-cases:**
  - Any account found to already run a phone-camera body scan or to have signed a scanning vendor: displacement, held for Vadim, standard copy never sent.
  - Investors and board observers: not at the company.
  - Corporate parents of a program (UnitedHealth Group, UnitedHealthcare, Optum): different segment and buyer; a separate future campaign.
  - Clinical research site networks (AMR Clinical): `icp-detail.md` §7 territory, not this campaign.
  - Companies headquartered outside the US (Myo, Toronto): not `nick`'s market.
  - Existing 3DLOOK customers (`existing_customer_excluded`): none on this list; the registry check still runs.
  - Mergers: an account announcing an acquisition or merger before send is paused.
- **People-level anti-cases:** the 12 FAIL rows in "Not the buyer" and held pool H.

### Vadim's decisions 2026-09-29 (standing, built in: not open questions)

1. **No headcount floor.** The "<50 employees" exclusion is removed from `icp-detail.md`. Segment revenue thresholds still apply (§1: $2M+).
2. **`cap_per_group: 50`**, the default for every campaign. **No waves:** everyone goes in one import file at the same time.
3. **Every function at an in-scope company gets a lane** (`clinical`, `product`, `operations`, `technical-integration`, `referral`), in priority tiers so the list is ordered. FAIL is reserved for wrong company, identity collisions and people not actually at the company.
4. **Referral-lane sequences carry no compliance line.** Every other lane gets one compliance line in message 2, the US variant verbatim from `compliance.md`.
5. **Former employers may be named in copy.**
6. **"112,100 scans in 2025 across all 3DLOOK customers" is cleared for cold copy** as 3DLOOK-wide scale only, and so is the 34,000-scan line with no client name and no geography. No 3DLOOK client is ever named.
7. **Nick's profile audit has not been done.** Acceptance risk accepted as is.

## ICP segment (icp-detail.md, verbatim)

### 1. Telehealth & GLP-1 / Weight Loss Programs

**What they are:** virtual clinics, telehealth platforms, coaching apps treating obesity / weight management, GLP-1 prescription platforms, longitudinal care & remote patient monitoring programs, cardiometabolic health platforms.

**Buyer titles (target for outbound):**
- Founder / CEO
- Chief Medical Officer / Medical Director
- Head of Clinical Operations
- Head of Member Engagement / Retention
- Head of Product / Product Manager
- CTO / Technical Lead
- Patient / Member Experience Director
- Growth & Revenue Operations
- Care Coordination Manager
- Head of Outcomes / Program Insights (когда важна outcomes-отчётность)

**Company size & revenue:** Series A through public, 50-5000 employees. **$2M+ annual revenue** — особенно компании, масштабирующие paid acquisition, onboarding и longitudinal-программы.

**Geo:** USA, Canada, UK, Germany, UAE, Australia.

**Business model:** subscription weight-loss programs, GLP-1 prescription platforms with ongoing care, insurance-supported obesity treatment, employer-sponsored metabolic health programs, cash-pay telehealth с repeat-engagement, digital wellness ecosystems (30/60/90-day+ программы).

**Pain points — Engagement & Retention:**
- Members drop off после onboarding, если нет visible progress
- Self-report и ручные progress-фото ощущаются "устаревшими" и слабее конкурентов
- Сложно поддерживать check-in cadence на 30/60/90 днях
- Нет стандартизированного способа показать body progress во времени

**Pain points — Operational:**
- Self-reported weight/BMI неточны и сложно верифицируемы
- Manual scale / progress-photo workflows — high-friction, легко подделать
- Manual intake замедляет масштабирование, нагружает клиническую команду
- Фрагментированные данные (self-report + весы + фото) блокируют чистый longitudinal tracking

**Pain points — Clinical, Risk & Growth:**
- GLP-1 назначения требуют надёжных baseline/follow-up метрик тела
- Небольшие реальные изменения теряются в измерительном шуме при слабой repeatability
- Растущий CAC при слабом engagement и раннем churn
- Payers/enterprise-партнёры всё больше ожидают измеримых, defensible outcomes

**KPIs they care about:** member retention / 6-month adherence, GLP-1 program ROI, lean mass preservation tracking, member engagement frequency, CAC vs LTV.

**Triggers (что заставляет покупать сейчас):**
- Недавний запуск GLP-1 программы
- Давление от payers показать outcomes
- Падение engagement-метрик после первых 90 дней
- Добавление body composition (не только веса) для дифференциации
- Расширение из one-time qualification в ongoing care модель

**Additional buying signals:** repeat check-ins 30/60/90+ дней как основная механика; retention/adherence как primary KPI; outcomes-отчётность payers/employers/insurers; care coordinators/member-success команды; инвестиции в member experience как дифференциатор; paid social с высоким CAC-давлением; международная экспансия.

**Positioning / hero message:** *"Make body progress more visible — before members drop off."* Альтернативы: "Trustworthy longitudinal body data for remote-first programs", "From two photos to structured body data, in under a minute", "Best-in-class repeatability for telehealth programs that depend on repeat scans."

**Key differentiator to lead with:** repeatability, не разовая точность — для программ, зависящих от повторных сканов, важнее не терять маленькие реальные изменения в измерительном шуме.

**Examples to target (verify status before outreach):**
- USA: Hims & Hers Health, Ro, LifeMD, Noom, Found, Calibrate, Sequence (WeightWatchers Clinic)
- UK: Voy, Juniper, Numan, Second Nature, Practice Plus Group
- Germany: Oviva
- Australia: Eucalyptus (incl. Juniper AU), Mosh
- UAE: Healthigo

**Competitor in their evaluation:** Prism Labs (primary), Bodygram (secondary).
